title.narrative: Regular monthly and quarterly reports delivered on time by BDA

comment.narrative: While BDA was rarely able to deliver regular reports on time, this did not affect supervision, as reports were usually submitted only slightly late and the World Bank/MTF Secretariat also received reports directly from the trust fund recipients, CFSI, MinLand and the ILO.

title.narrative: Grievances registered related to delivery of project benefits addressed (%)
Program partnerships forged by BDA with other organizations

comment.narrative: This was seen as a measure of the institutional maturity of BDA, which commenced operations with funding exclusively from the MTF.

title.narrative: Community-wide meetings achieve at least 60% participation of households

comment.narrative: This target turned out to be unrealistic, reflecting on one hand that some people did not respond well to the MILF/BDA for political reasons, and therefore the difficulty they had in convincing people to come to community meetings but also some weaknesses in facilitation/social mobilization. BDA reports that on average around 30% of households were represented in community-wide meetings. Sometimes it was more, sometimes less. The People's Organizations were usually made up of 25 people, representing 25 households. The average population in a Barangay in the Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao is 1,500, which translates to 300 households. This means from the PO members alone, 8 percent of households were represented at all meetings.

title.narrative: Training sessions provided to people's organizations
Communities with improved local infrastructure facilities and/or livelihood activities implemented by the project

comment.narrative: This reflects the total number of communities where the project has been active, either through the provision of community infrastructure, or livelihood support.

title.narrative: Communities with sub-project investments that match one of top three identified priorities
Community members who reported participation in a collective effort and also reported improved well being
Community members perceiving people's organizations as a functional organization
Number of PO members trained in training sessions
Beneficiaries that feel project investments reflected their needs (percentage)
Local communities, poeple's organizations and local government units perceive BDA to be a credible development partner

comment.narrative: This data reflects community perceptions of the BDA and is based on levels of satisfaction with the performance of BDA in the MTF-RDP. The views of POs are included in the community sample and the views of LGUs were captured through FGDs and KIIs in all three impact assessments (2009, 2012 and 2017).

title.narrative: Percentage of sub-projects with adequate workmanship

comment.narrative: Based on a random sample of subprojects assessed by the World Bank's rural engineer.

comment.narrative: Data was not collected by BDA in the last two years of implementation.

title.narrative: Number of people's organizations with female officers

comment.narrative: Officers are senior members of the PO, including President, Vice-President, Treasurer and Secretary.

title.narrative: Communities report better access to basic services (time, distance and cost)

comment.narrative: The sample for this indicator here is community members as a whole in target villages, not just direct beneficiaries of the project.

title.narrative: Increase in number of community members reporting trust in other members/groups within their community

comment.narrative: This indicator measures an increase in the net trust over the previous 12 months in people from other ethnic and religious groups. This measure takes the difference between those who reported that trust had increased a lot or a little as against those who reported that trust had decreased a lot or a little compared to a year earlier.

title.narrative: Beneficiaries experiencing greater security in project areas (%)
The economic internal rate of return for community sub-projects will be at or beyond 12%.

comment.narrative: EIRR analysis was undertaken in 2009 and 2013, which showed that the project was roughly on track to have an EIRR of 12% or above. Financial rates of return were as follows. Low: over 6% for hydro-tillers/water pumps and high: 20% for coco grills. Updated cost/benefit data from the last few years of the project was not readily available, but it can be reasonably assumed that economic rates of return would be positive and most likely higher than captured in the 2013 analysis.

Number of project-facilitated meetings conducted without incidents of conflict
Number of BDA and Sajahatra Bangsamoro Project Management Team staff participating in capacity-building sessions

comment.narrative: In addition to the numbers noted above, the project also provided capacity-building sessions to 30 members of the joint Task Forces on Camps Transformation.

title.narrative: Increase in number of community members confident that the BDA/MILF and the government of the Philippines can work together for the benefit of the community

comment.narrative: The impact assessment asked a series of questions about the impact of the MTF-RDP on the following: (i) MTF-RDP shows that the MILF and the government can work together for the good of the community; (ii) MTF-RDP encourages communication between the MILF and theovernment; (iii) MTF-RDP helps to diffuse tensions between the MILF and the government; (iv) MTF-RDP improves the relationship of the MILF and the government; (v) MTRF-RDP improves the trust between the MILF and the government; and (vi) MTF-RDP will help bring about peace in Mindanao. Between 53-61 percent of respondents either agreed or strongly agreed with these statements. The impact assessment was supposed to include recall questions to track changes in views on this topic, but in an oversight this was not covered by the research firm. The qualitative data shows very strong benefits on this point from the project.

title.narrative: Increase in number of community members who think their opinion counts in what needs to be done in their community

comment.narrative: This indicator measures the increase in the percentage of community members who strongly agreed or agreed that their opinion counts in what needs to be done in the community before and after the project against those who disagreed or strongly disagreed.

title.narrative: Increase in number of community members reporting communications with members of a different group (ethnic, religious or different sub-village)

comment.narrative: This calculates the net result of people who responded that communication had increased a little or a lot over those who said it had decreased a little or a lot for different ethnic and religious groups and people from different sub-villages (sitios).

title.narrative: Number of common facilities constructed and being used by the community

comment.narrative: The nature of business activities in some locations was such that common service facilities were not required in all 11 locations, but only 8.

title.narrative: Increase in income for those who secure wage employment

comment.narrative: As noted above, this activity was dropped.

title.narrative: Increase in income for those who start a new enterprise

comment.narrative: The percentage increase in income at the closing of the project was based on an estimation made by the ILO, which was providing technical support to the BDA for the implementation of this component. However, even the ILO acknowledges that this was based on incomplete data, and therefore the robustness of this figure is questionable. An independent impact evaluation was planned, which was meant to measure the increase in income of households, but this ran into problems as well, and no data on income was collected. It did confirm however that households perceived a small increase in income, or increase in savings, due to the activities of the new community enterprise.

title.narrative: Number of people who receive employment skills training

comment.narrative: Employment skills training was dropped in the last year of implementation so the project could focus attention on the sustainability of the 42 community enterprise groups.

title.narrative: Percentage of those who receive employment skills training who secure wage employment

comment.narrative: As noted above, this activity was dropped.

title.narrative: Number of people receiving entrepreneurship training and support
Percentage of beneficiaries who receive entrepreneurship training and support who establish a new enterprise

comment.narrative: The enterprises set up were community enterprises, with several households joining one enterprise. Individual households did not set up businesses through this project.
